correctness.rationale: For f normalized by Σ|f_j|=1 and a=max|f_j|, coordinate deletion j has inverse missing coordinate x_j=−Σ_{i≠j}f_i y_i/f_j and norm max(1,(1−a_j)/a_j), giving Δ=max(1,(1−a)/a). Finite-dimensional 1-injectivity of ℓ∞^N and Hahn–Banach equate absolute and ambient minimal projection constants. Every projection is I−u⊗f with f(u)=1; write t_j=f_j u_j. Its row norm R_j=|1−t_j|+(1−a_j)|t_j|/a_j, so for a<1/2, R_j≥1+((1−2a_j)/a_j)|t_j|. Σ t_j=1 gives L≥1+(Σ a_j/(1−2a_j))^−1, equality by positive balanced t_j; a≥1/2 gives λ=1. The inequality Σ a_j/(1−2a_j)≤1/(1−2a) implies λ≥2−2a and Δ≤λ/(2−λ), with equality only if all nonzero a_j=a. Independently verified six exact rational-weight families with zero coefficients and both equality regimes. The result does not assert a sharp unrestricted Banach–Mazur distance.
residual_risks: The complex-case Hahn–Banach extension and row-sum extremization are valid, but reliance on standard injective ℓ∞ property is explicit.

value.rationale: The precise dimension-free relation quantitatively calibrates best coordinate deletion against an intrinsic projection constant for all real and complex finite-dimensional hyperplanes. It improves the older real-domain distortion estimate and proves an exact positive-weight equality classification, with sharp order near λ=1 and extension to the full 1≤λ<2 interval. This is a natural nonlinear geometric comparison; the sharpness is carefully restricted to the meaningful coordinate-frame invariant, not overstated for Banach–Mazur distance.
residual_risks: Although λ can be classical, the usefulness of the specific Δ bound is that it is constructive; unrestricted optimal Banach–Mazur sharpness is not established.

limitations: Projection constant absolute, Δ best of coordinate-deletion maps, not arbitrary linear isomorphisms.
